content:
Mica (infra): Heads-up — we saw another big cost blip overnight from autoscale bursts in us-west-2.
Jonah: saw that in the dashboard, looks like burst scaled to 2.1x steady and stayed ~45m.
Mica (infra): baseline steady GPUs ~1,200 GPU-hours/day for primary fleets. burst added about 800 GPU-hours yesterday (~40% uplift).
Priyanka: is that from a bad cooldown or a noisy metric?
Jonah: a mix — queue_length spiked due to a traffic storm from one customer + kube event pushed replicas up before cache warmed.
Sam (SRE lead): can we tighten guardrails so bursts can't exceed 50% of steady for more than 15m without manual ack? current config is too loose.
Mica (infra): proposed quick patch: reduce max_burst_ratio from 2.5 -> 1.5 and add a burst_budget per-region. also bump cooldown to 10m.
Jonah: agree, happy to apply to canary region first (us-west-2). snippet we tested locally:```yaml
autoscaler:
  policy: target_queue_length
  target: 50
  max_burst_ratio: 1.5
  burst_budget_minutes: 15
  cooldown_seconds: 600
  require_manual_ack_after_minutes: 15
```
Priyanka: add a hard cap too: max_gpus_per_cluster: 400 in us-west-2, so even multiple bursts don't blow budget.
Dave (finance): number check — if burst ratio drops to 1.5 and we hit same traffic, estimated savings ~28%/week on excess GPUs (~$32k/week). we need that for Q2 forecast.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for autoscaler-config v2 -> us-west-2 at 1718606123
Jonah: can we also switch metric from raw queue_length to p95 latency + queue to avoid reacting to short spikes?
Mica (infra): good call — p95 latency + queue_length (weighted) should be more stable. I'll draft rule: score = 0.6*p95_latency_ms + 0.4*queue_len. threshold tuned to steady traffic.
Sam (SRE lead): put a listener on alerts: if burst_budget used > 80% for 2 consecutive days, auto-create a paging ticket to infra-oncall.
Priyanka: and schedule an infra sync with product for expected seasonal windows (holidays, new feature launches). July spike last year was predictable; add schedule-based capacity too.
Dave (finance): remind me — what's our steady vs peak GPU-hour projection for Black Friday style event? need numbers for procurement.
Mica (infra): rough projection: steady 1,200 GPU-hrs/day -> peak 3,000 GPU-hrs/day (including spikes) for Black Friday scenario. With tighter burst cap, peak moves to ~2,400 -> procurement needs 2.4k baseline or 3k reserved with auto-burst.
Jonah: will roll the canary patch now, monitor 2 hours, then promote if stable.
Priyanka: logging note — record burst events with reason tag (cache_miss|customer_storm|deploy|network_issue) so we can triage cause quickly.
Sam (SRE lead): assign follow-ups: Mica to apply config and update runbook; Priyanka to add logging tags; Dave to update cost forecast. we reconvene in 48h. :thumbsup:
Mica (infra): applying patch to canary, will paste rollout logs here.
deploy-bot: rollout completed to canary at 1718606823
Mica (infra): initial 30m looks good — bursts limited, costs flatter. will watch longer and then promote to prod.
